output.brief:
The shortfall is mostly not Admissions' doing. Applications, admits and student quality all rose; what fell was the share of admitted students who enrolled (41.8% to 34.3%).

That fall sits almost entirely in the two scholarship tiers whose awards the Board cut for Fall 2026: Dean's ($14,000 to $9,000) and Merit ($9,000 to $5,000). Their enrolment rates dropped about 13 points, 320 of the 330 lost students. Presidential (award unchanged) and no-scholarship students barely moved. The Board assumed little effect, from a 2021 estimate; that looks wrong. Regular-decision answers were slow, but early-action students, whose decisions came on time, fell by the same amount (7.4 vs 7.5 points), so lateness doesn't explain the loss. I'm about 85% confident the scholarship change is the main cause.

Still open: competitor offers, net revenue, and whether the portal lost documents.

Next: don't replace the director on this basis. Take the schedule back to the finance committee with a costed proposal to restore Dean's and Merit awards, showing net revenue both ways, before award letters go out. Also set a regular-decision turnaround target, and check the missing-transcript reports before invoking the vendor clause.
